gen-gf-the-girl-next-door-fs-asap: Loose, hand-lettered warmth, with a big lowercase and unshaded strokes. Asap steps in as a sans whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals in height, giving the handwriting a tidy, professional partner.
gen-gf-the-girl-next-door-fs-epilogue: A broad, hook-shaped c gives The Girl Next Door its handwritten, personal charm. Epilogue, a sans-serif of curvy, wire-thin monoline letters, reads loose and approachable as the text runs on paragraph after paragraph.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-graduate: Turret Road brings round, parenthesis-like forms and a pen-like line of constant weight. Graduate adds dignified, bookish space between its letters, and that generous breathing room is what the pair does best.
gen-gf-yomogi-fs-bespoke-sans: A crescent-wrench c, opened wide, gives Yomogi its hand-drawn friendliness, with curves and straights all sharing a single width. Bespoke Sans sharpens it all with refined, generously spaced curve ends.
gen-shadows-into-light-satoshi: Satoshi reads tall, open and approachable, with an e that never squeezes shut. Shadows Into Light handles the casual, chalk-crowded handwriting, while Satoshi, a sans-serif, supplies uniform strokes and a soaring x-height.
gen-gf-metamorphous-fs-quicksand: Metamorphous spaces itself generously, with a high-set midline and mild stress. Quicksand, a sans-serif of rounded lowercase bowls and identical bar thickness, keeps the text feeling light and approachable line after line.
gen-gf-baumans-lora: Blunt, quirky and uniform, Baumans pairs a crescent-wrench c opened wide with strokes that never thin or thicken. Lora, a serif, reads warmly, its hairline thinning gentle and its c welcoming.
gen-gf-bellota-text-lora: No calligraphic shading, just open rounded forms: that is Bellota Text. Bellota Text delivers display punch with evenly weighted rounds, while Lora handles the quieter work of text, its bowls shifting gently in weight.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-lora: Lora, a serif with mild pen-like weight variation, settles in beside Shantell Sans, whose wide-mouthed, bent-paperclip letters never swell. Expressive against literary is the whole appeal, and it shows instantly.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-gambetta: Sniglet is level and quiet, with no accents of weight. Gambetta, a serif with wide channels into each counter, reads graceful and bookish as the text unfolds, with weight shifts that stay noticeable but mild.
